name: Future Islands
label: 4AD
lede: Three friends from eastern North Carolina played a thousand shows in ten years before one four-minute Letterman spot, all chest-thumps and a growl, made the whole world ask who Sam Herring was.

eras.title: Art Lord and the white suit
eras.text: Before Future Islands there was Art Lord & the Self-Portraits, a performance-art band from East Carolina University in Greenville. Sam Herring and Gerrit Welmers had been friends since eighth grade in Morehead City, and art-school classmate William Cashion had helped Herring cram for an art history exam. That was the whole plan.

years.h: Art Lord & the Self-Portraits debut on Valentine's Day
years.p: The band's first show, at a Greenville house called Soccer Moms' House, is remembered as tumultuous. Sam Herring performs in character as Locke Ernst-Frost, a narcissistic German artist in a 1970s white suit.
years.xp:
The character's name mashed up the philosopher John Locke, the painter Max Ernst and the poet Robert Frost. The line-up: Herring on vocals, Gerrit Welmers on keyboards, William Cashion on guitar then bass, Adam Beeby on rhythmic keyboards and Kymia Nawabi on percussion and backing vocals.

Herring later said he fell in love with performance art at 17. Art Lord was where that came out.

years.h: Kymia Nawabi leaves Art Lord to finish her degree
years.p: Kymia Nawabi, a senior, quits Art Lord & the Self-Portraits in mid-2003 to work on her graduation project. She later painted the covers for five Future Islands records.

years.h: Adam Beeby leaves Greenville; Art Lord ends
years.p: When keyboardist Adam Beeby moves away from Greenville, Art Lord & the Self-Portraits falls apart.

eras.title: Future Shoes, Already Islands
eras.text: Herring, Welmers and Cashion regrouped as Future Islands to keep a tour date, added a drum machine player, and started cutting records cheaply and fast. Then Herring hit a wall and left town for a year.

years.h: Future Islands' first show: an anti-Valentine's party
years.p: Formed to fill a tour slot with alt-country band The Texas Governor, Future Islands plays its first show at an anti-Valentine's Day party at a Greenville house called Turducken. Erick Murillo plays electronic drums.
years.xp: The name was a compromise. The two finalists were Future Shoes and Already Islands, so they combined them. William Cashion has told that story many times.

years.h: Little Advances EP, self-released
years.p: Recorded in March 2006, Future Islands' first EP is self-released.

years.h: Sam Herring drops out of college over substance abuse
years.p: Sam Herring leaves East Carolina University in June 2006. He later said he got sucked into the partying, moved to Asheville, and it took about a year to get his act together.

years.h: Wave Like Home cut in three days at a skate shop
years.p: Future Islands records its first album at the Backdoor Skateshop in Greenville with Chester Endersby Gwazda. William Cashion said they made it in three days and spent a month mixing.

years.h: Erick Murillo leaves; Future Islands becomes a trio
years.p: Drummer Erick Murillo leaves after Halloween 2007. Future Islands carries on as three, with a drum machine.

eras.title: Baltimore, a torn knee and a broken heart
eras.text: Encouraged by Dan Deacon, the trio moved to Baltimore for cheap rent and easy drives to New York, Philadelphia and D.C. They toured relentlessly, Herring's long relationship ended, and that breakup became the first of two albums on Thrill Jockey.

years.h: Future Islands moves to Baltimore
years.p: Pushed by [[Dan Deacon|8dd73d1a-0424-4581-af8c-ade3edb44c5a]] and Benny Boeldt of Adventure, William Cashion moves to Baltimore in November 2007, Sam Herring in January 2008, and Gerrit Welmers later that year.

years.h: Wave Like Home · Upset The Rhythm
years.p: London's Upset The Rhythm releases Future Islands' debut album, a year after it was recorded, with a Kymia Nawabi cover.

years.h: Sam Herring's long relationship ends after back-to-back tours
years.p: After consecutive national tours, Sam Herring's long-term relationship ends. The breakup becomes the backbone of In Evening Air.

years.h: Sam Herring tackled by a drunk fan in Paris, tears his ACL
years.p: On tour with the Dan Deacon Ensemble behind Bromst, Sam Herring is tackled by a drunken spectator in Paris. The knee turns out to have a torn ACL; he has surgery in February 2010 and plays Amoeba that June in a brace.

years.h: Double Dagger's Bruce Willen gets Future Islands to Thrill Jockey
years.p: Bruce Willen of Baltimore's [[Double Dagger|6b35f310-3ba2-4fef-afa2-33f5cc706652]] passes a four-song demo to Thrill Jockey: Tin Man, Walking Through That Door, Long Flight and As I Fall. The label signs them.

years.h: In Evening Air, recorded in a Baltimore living room
years.p: Future Islands' Thrill Jockey debut was recorded in July 2009 in a living room in Baltimore's Marble Hill with Chester Endersby Gwazda. Its songs trace Sam Herring's breakup.
years.xp: The same year brought the In the Fall EP with Katrina Ford of Celebration, The Post Office Chapel Wave EP with [[No Age|55821c25-bd47-4f67-baf8-17ccd2cf1c86]] and [[Beach House|d5cc67b8-1cc4-453b-96e8-44487acdebea]]'s Victoria Legrand, and Undressed, recorded July 7, 2010 at Mobtown Studios.

years.h: On the Water, written in a borrowed house by the sea
years.p: Future Islands wrote and recorded On the Water in ten days in a friend's house in Elizabeth City, North Carolina. [[Jenn Wasner|c7616574-4d5d-425d-b45e-5b9392e8661c]] of [[Wye Oak|3c8ff4c9-b5b9-4e78-ad9d-5157c323de24]] duets on The Great Fire.
years.xp: It wasn't all calm. Sam Herring recalled someone from the label hanging around during writing, talking about deadlines, and asking whether they could not talk business while writing a song.

years.h: Future Islands breaks with Thrill Jockey
years.p: After a year touring On the Water, Future Islands cuts ties with Thrill Jockey. The next singles come out on Upset The Rhythm and Famous Class.

eras.title: Seasons
eras.text: After five straight years on the road, the band disappeared into the woods to write, signed to 4AD, and made the record that changed everything. One TV spot turned a hard-working cult band into a worldwide story, and Herring's body paid for the tour that followed.

years.h: Future Islands writes in a rented North Carolina hunting cabin
years.p: From February to July 2013 the band writes in a rural hunting cabin. Sam Herring said they demoed 24 or 25 songs, wrote about eight in the cabin, and three made the record.

years.h: Singles recorded in Hurley, New York with Chris Coady
years.p: Future Islands records at Dreamland Recording Studios in Hurley, New York with producer Chris Coady, under a new three-album deal with 4AD.

years.cap: Late Show with David Letterman, March 3, 2014
years.src: Wikipedia · Late Show with David Letterman
years.h: Letterman: Seasons (Waiting on You) goes viral
years.p: Future Islands plays Seasons (Waiting on You) on the Late Show with David Letterman. Sam Herring's chest-beating, hip-swiveling performance becomes the most-viewed video on the show's YouTube channel.
years.xp: Herring danced, pounded his chest and dropped into a guttural growl, and the clip spread everywhere within days. David Letterman came over afterward delighted. Critics later called it one of the great live TV performances.

years.h: Singles, Future Islands' 4AD debut
years.p: Three weeks after Letterman, Singles is out on 4AD with a collage cover by Beth Hoeckel.

q: Basically, I was four for four.
years.h: Sam Herring diagnosed with Reinke's edema
years.p: Sam Herring is diagnosed with Reinke's edema, a swelling of the vocal cords. He listed its four causes, acid reflux, smoking, talking too much and misusing the voice, and said he had all four.
years.xp: To get through shows he leaned harder on the growl, which became one of his trademarks.

years.h: Sam Herring collapses at an airport, plays Primavera Sound anyway
years.p: Exhausted, Sam Herring passes out at an airport during Primavera Sound weekend. Medics revive him, and he still plays the festival that night.

years.h: Seasons named song of the year by Pitchfork and NME
years.p: Pitchfork, NME, Consequence of Sound and the Village Voice's Pazz & Jop critics' poll all name Seasons (Waiting on You) the best song of 2014.

years.h: The Chase / Haunted by You, recorded with Jim Eno
years.p: Future Islands releases a two-song single recorded in Austin with [[Spoon|84eac621-1c5a-49a1-9500-555099c6e184]]'s [[Jim Eno|402a60a2-65cb-4f79-870f-7f9ffdf3bb20]] at Public Hi-Fi.

years.h: Sam Herring tears a meniscus at Red Rocks opening for Morrissey
years.p: Opening for [[Morrissey|013fa897-86db-41d3-8e9f-386c8a34f4e6]] at Red Rocks Amphitheatre, Sam Herring tears his meniscus doing a knee drop. He finishes the last four months of the Singles tour on it.

eras.title: The long road after the viral clip
eras.text: Future Islands turned a moment into a career: a drummer on record, big-name producers, festival stages and TV again. Herring kept writing about love coming apart, most nakedly about a long-distance relationship lost to lockdown.

years.h: Secret shows as The Hidden Haven, This Old House, Chirping Bush
years.p: After writing in a four-story beach house in Avon, on the Outer Banks, Future Islands tests the new songs at shows under fake names. Chirping Bush came from Gerrit Welmers' dream about birds stuck in a bush.

years.h: The Far Field, with Debbie Harry and a real drummer
years.p: Recorded at Sunset Sound in Los Angeles with John Congleton, The Far Field features Debbie Harry of [[Blondie|4d2956d1-a3f7-44bb-9a41-67563e1a0c94]] and new drummer Michael Lowry of [[Lake Trout|08b14860-14fb-454e-a83d-8178174d7d90]]. Kymia Nawabi paints the cover.
years.xp: The title and themes come from the poet Theodore Roethke. Michael Lowry, from the Baltimore bands Lake Trout and Mt. Royal, became a core member after years of Future Islands using touring drummers.

years.h: As Long as You Are, released mid-pandemic
years.p: Future Islands' third 4AD album arrives with For Sure, which later lands in the MLB The Show 21 soundtrack.

years.h: Back on the Late Show: King of Sweden for Colbert
years.p: Eight years after Letterman, Future Islands returns to the Ed Sullivan Theater to play King of Sweden on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert.

years.h: Future Islands opens for Weezer on Indie Rock Road Trip
years.p: Future Islands supports [[Weezer|6fe07aa5-fec0-4eca-a456-f29bff451b04]] on several dates of the 2023 Indie Rock Road Trip tour.

years.h: People Who Aren't There Anymore, a lockdown breakup album
years.p: Written and recorded through the COVID-19 pandemic, Future Islands' seventh album tracks the end of Sam Herring's long-distance relationship across worldwide lockdowns.

years.h: From a Hole in the Floor to a Fountain of Youth: rarities
years.p: Future Islands schedules a compilation of deep cuts, rarities and live tracks for May 22, 2026, with a North American tour that month.
